governing_question: What is the real boost-switch-short fault stress from the ACTUAL schematic and fault-current paths, and does the AR-VERIFY ~586.7 V device stress hold?

board.topology: Classic CCM boost PFC: passive diode bridge U1 -> boost inductor U8 -> low-side switch U9 (drain=a1, source=PFC_BUS_MINUS) -> shunt U12 -> bus caps on PFC_BUS_PLUS_390V/PFC_BUS_MINUS; boost diode U10 anode=a1, cathode=hv_plus.

named_topology.note: Net membership is verbatim from source-manifest.json bridge.nets (raw/netlist_fault_loop.json).

claim_under_test.claim_origin: AR-VERIFY attempt-001 inputs.json terminal_voltages.bus_fault_boost_switch_short_v and REPORT.md:76; constructed in raw/compute_ar_verify.py:415 as round(v_bus + v_peak_132, 2) with v_bus=400 and v_peak_132=186.676.
claim_under_test.verdict: DOES NOT HOLD AS A SINGLE-FAULT DEVICE STRESS
claim_under_test.verdict_basis: no net on this board is the series sum of the bus potential and the line peak; see fault_paths.

conducting_elements_in_order: NTC U4 or bypass relay U5 (l2->ac1)
A_boost_switch_short.loop: mains L -> F1 -> CMC L1(1)/L2(4) -> U4/U5 -> bridge AC1 -> upper diode -> bridge PLUS -> U8 -> a1 -> shorted U9 -> PFC_BUS_MINUS -> U12 -> bridge MINUS -> lower diode -> bridge AC2 -> CMC N2(3)/N1(2) -> mains N.

limiting_impedance.inductor_L: 180 uH +/-20% limits di/dt only until Isat (43 A typ, |dL/L|<30%)
limiting_impedance.line_source_impedance_note: NOT ESTABLISHED anywhere in the tree; sets the post-saturation current.

A_boost_switch_short.bus_capacitor_reason: After the U9 short, node a1 = PFC_BUS_MINUS. Boost diode U10 (anode a1, cathode hv_plus) is reverse-biased by the full bus voltage. hv_plus has no other path to the fault: its only board-side connections are U10.K, c1..c4/c_hf +, output U52.1, bleeder U53, and the U20..U24 vsense divider. So the 179 J stored in the bus bank does NOT discharge into the shorted switch.

B_boost_diode_short.fault: U10 K (hv_plus) shorted to U10 A1/A2 (a1).
B_boost_diode_short.loop: PFC_BUS_PLUS_390V -> shorted U10 -> a1 -> U8 -> bridge PLUS; and PFC_BUS_MINUS -> U12 -> bridge MINUS. The bus bank sits across the bridge DC output, in reverse, through U8.

standing_state_switch_off.bridge_diode_max_reverse_basis: A standard bridge clamps each AC terminal to [MINUS-Vf, PLUS]; the bridge's own low-side diode prevents an AC node reaching the opposite line peak, so no bridge diode sees V_bus + V_line. Max single-diode reverse is ~V_bus (~400 V).
standing_state_switch_off.current: zero except leakage: the bridge blocks reverse, and U9 is off.

if_switch_conducts.mechanism: The controller (U11) still sees a 400 V bus on VSENSE, so nothing signals it to stop; if U9 continues to be driven, hv_plus -> shorted U10 -> a1 -> U9(on) -> PFC_BUS_MINUS is a direct bus-capacitor discharge.
if_switch_conducts.caveat: This internal loop is NOT seen by the AC fuse F1.

C_why_586_7_is_not_a_real_node.argument: Every bridge AC terminal is clamped by the bridge's own devices: the upper device (AC->PLUS) prevents an AC node rising above PLUS, and the lower device (MINUS->AC) prevents it falling below MINUS. So no AC node can be V_PLUS + V_line above MINUS; the largest span any bridge device blocks is PLUS - MINUS = V_bus.
C_why_586_7_is_not_a_real_node.consequence: 586.676 V would require one AC node at bus+ (400 V) and the other at the opposite line peak (-186.7 V) simultaneously. The second condition is blocked by that node's own lower clamp. Reaching it needs an *additional* open-circuit clamp fault, not the described short fault; therefore 586.676 V corresponds to no real device node on this board under the traced faults.
C_why_586_7_is_not_a_real_node.residual_note: The only way a bridge device could legitimately see V_bus + V_line is if it sits between the line and the bus with no intervening clamp (a bridgeless/totem-pole stage). This board is a classic diode-bridge boost, so it does not.

bus_discharge_natural.note: Passive bleed only on this candidate; no active bus-discharge component in the netlist.

peak_switch_short_current.status: PARAMETRIC - the gating input (line/source impedance) is unknown
peak_switch_short_current.unknown_input: AC source/line impedance (R, X); also the NTC state at the fault instant.

device_energy_switch_short.why: The line-fed fault energy is the integral of the fault voltage and current over the fuse clearing time. Both the current (line impedance) and the clearing time (F1 pre-arcing I2t, not captured) are unknown. Not zero-filled.

interruption.device: F1 = Schurter 0034.3129, FST 5x20mm, 16 A / 250 V, time-lag; holder U2 = 0031.2510
interruption.is_switch_short_interrupted: YES, in principle - F1 is in the line-fed loop, so a line-frequency fault current flows through it. Whether it clears before the bridge (IFSM 350 A / I2t 510 A2s) or the PCB is damaged is NOT established (F1 pre-arcing I2t not captured).
interruption.is_bus_cap_discharge_interrupted: NO - the bus-cap discharge loop (caps -> U10 -> U9 -> shunt) is internal and does not pass through F1; nothing on the board interrupts it.

line_frequency_vs_cap_discharge.line_frequency_fault_current: rectified 120 Hz current through bridge/L/switch-short, sourced by the mains; timescale set by F1 (ms to tens of ms); bounded by the source impedance.
line_frequency_vs_cap_discharge.capacitor_discharge_current: 2240 uF through ~50 mohm, tau ~116 us; only occurs (a) on a diode short with the switch conducting, or (b) an external load; not on a bare switch short.

mov_assessment.statement: The MOV is NOT in either internal fault loop. Neither bus rail (PFC_BUS_PLUS_390V, PFC_BUS_MINUS) reaches its terminals; it clamps the line only. Its clamp voltage is therefore not admissible evidence for this fault and no MOV clamp figure is used anywhere in this assessment.

protection_recommendations.bridge_device_voltage_class: On the actual board the rectifier U1 is already 1000 V. If a candidate replaces U1 with an active bridge, the single-fault blocking requirement is the bus (~400 V) on a diode short and the line peak (186.7 V) on a switch short; a 600 V device gives ~1.5x on the 400 V case. The 586.7 V figure does not force an 800/1000 V device, because it is not a single-fault stress.
protection_recommendations.switch_current_energy_withstand: The switch-short case is a CURRENT/ENERGY fault, not a voltage fault. The switch is the failed element; the surviving bridge sees IFSM 350 A / I2t 510 A2s, so the fault must be cleared well inside those.
required_additions: Capture F1's pre-arcing I2t / time-current curve and coordinate it against the bridge IFSM/I2t and the prospective fault current.
Add protection for the internal bus-cap discharge path (bus-side fuse, DC breaker, crowbar, or a controller fast overcurrent shutdown); the AC fuse cannot interrupt it.
Resolve the AC source/line impedance to bound the prospective fault current.
protection_recommendations.crowbar_or_clamp_note: A bus-side clamp/crowbar could bound the diode-short discharge; it is a design addition, not present on the candidate.

assumptions_marked.assumption: bus setpoint is 400 V (worst case); the board net is named PFC_BUS_PLUS_390V
assumptions_marked.impact: energy scales as V^2 (179.2 J at 400 V vs 170.4 J at 390 V)

assumptions_marked.assumption: fault occurs while running at full load, NTC bypass relay U5 closed (NTC out of loop)
assumptions_marked.impact: if the relay is open, the cold 10 ohm NTC limits the line-fed fault current to ~19 A

assumptions_marked.assumption: post-saturation loop resistance known part = 30 mohm (L DCR max 20 + shunt 10)
